chunks: if you grieve over your son, certainly it is the consequence of the blood relationship; but if you endure, then Allāh provides recompense for every affliction.

key_terms.الرَّحِمُ: Kinship or blood relationship; the bond of family ties.
key_terms.الصَّبْرُ: Patience or endurance in the face of hardship.
key_terms.خَلَفٌ: Recompense, substitute, or something given in return.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of grieving for a child and how does patience bring divine recompense?
ai.summary: In this famous address to Ash‘ath ibn Qays, Imam Ali (AS) validates the natural human emotion of grief as a sign of deep kinship (rahim) while elevating it through conscious patience (sabr). This dual approach reflects the Shia theological balance between emotional authenticity and spiritual resilience, promising divine recompense (khalaf) that transcends worldly loss. The narration underscores the concept that enduring trials with patience transforms personal sorrow into a means of spiritual elevation and divine reward.
